rows.title: Ottawa imposing import limits, tariffs on some canned vegetables
rows.summary: The federal government announced a final safeguard measure on certain canned vegetable imports after the Canadian International Trade Tribunal found that rising imports were seriously injuring Canadian producers. The measure is a tariff rate quota: the first 13 million kilograms of imports in year one enter without the extra tariff, while imports above that amount face a 50% tariff. Over time the quota rises to just over 13.5 million kg and the over-quota tariff falls to 40%, with the measure running from Dec. 1 to June 17, 2029. Imports from Mexico, Chile, Israel, Colombia, Korea, Panama, Peru and some developing countries are exempt, and parts of the quota are reserved for the United States, the European Union and Thailand. It replaces a 10% provisional surtax in place since June, and the tribunal will run a process early next year to let parties seek exclusions for products not made in Canada.
rows.fact: Ottawa will apply a tariff rate quota of 13 million kg in year one, with a 50% tariff on canned vegetable imports above the quota, from Dec. 1 until June 17, 2029. Several free-trade partners and developing countries are exempt, and shares of the quota are set aside for the US, EU and Thailand.
rows.why: 정부가 수입 급증으로부터 국내 생산자를 보호하기 위해 '관세할당(TRQ)'이라는 무역 구제 수단을 어떻게 쓰는지, 그리고 그 대가로 소비자 물가가 오를 수 있다는 보호무역의 장단점을 이해하는 데 도움이 됩니다.
rows.why_en: It shows how a government uses a tariff rate quota to shield domestic producers from an import surge, and the trade-off between protecting jobs and raising prices for consumers.
rows.term_def: A two-level tariff system: a set quantity of imports (the quota) comes in at a low or zero extra tariff, and anything above that quantity is charged a much higher tariff, limiting imports without banning them.
rows.note: Today's policy item (federal tariff/trade measure, Department of Finance announcement Nov 25 ET; CP story 3:16 p.m. EST Nov 25 = Nov 26 KST). Quota (13,000,000 kg), 50% falling to 40% over-quota tariff, Dec. 1, 2026 to June 17, 2029 term, exemptions, reserved allocations and CITT exclusion inquiry (by Feb. 1, 2027) all checked against the Finance Canada release 'Canada moves forward with final safeguard measure on canned vegetables imports' (canada.ca, Nov 25, 2026). Earlier 10% provisional surtax (June 19, 2026) confirmed from Finance Canada's June release. Not a repeat of the covered list. StatCan's Sept payroll/job vacancies release (Nov 26, 8:30 ET) was considered but its Daily page could not be fetched.

opinion.title: The rising cost of food: New tariffs on canned vegetables are not helping matters
opinion.author: Renaud Brossard
opinion.summary: The free-market Montreal Economic Institute argues that Ottawa's tariffs on imported canned vegetables (the 10% provisional surtax that the new quota system replaces) will push up grocery bills at a time when living costs are already high. It cites Statistics Canada data showing overall consumer prices up 3.2% over 12 months, store-bought food up 4.3%, and canned vegetables and vegetable products up 4.6%. Brossard says the government contradicts its own cost-of-living message by taxing food, and that low-income families will be hit hardest. The MEI calls for more trade liberalization rather than protectionist measures.
opinion.why: 관세가 결국 누가 부담하는지, 그리고 국내 산업 보호와 소비자 물가 부담 사이의 상충 관계를 비판적 시각에서 생각해 보게 해 줍니다.
opinion.why_en: It makes readers think about who really pays for a tariff and the conflict between protecting an industry and keeping food affordable.

rows.title: US third-quarter GDP growth revised sharply higher
rows.summary: The Commerce Department's Bureau of Economic Analysis raised its estimate of US third-quarter growth to a 4.3% annualized rate from 3.4% in the first estimate, the fastest pace in three years and well above the 3.5% economists polled by Reuters had expected. The upgrade came mainly from stronger consumer spending, revised to a 4.2% rate, and business investment, with equipment spending tied heavily to artificial intelligence growing at a 21.8% rate. Final sales to private domestic purchasers, a measure of underlying demand that leaves out inventories, trade and government, sped up to 5.8%, the fastest since 2021. Reuters noted that spending is being led by higher-income households whose wealth rose with stocks, while others are saving less and drawing down savings as wage gains sometimes trail inflation. Economists warned that the AI investment boom could cool as investors look harder at AI company valuations.
rows.fact: Real GDP grew at a 4.3% annual rate in Q3 2026, revised up from 3.4%, after 2.2% in Q2. Consumer spending was revised to 4.2% from 3.8%, and gross domestic income rose at a 4.4% rate. Corporate profits from current production rose $206.0 billion in the quarter.
rows.outlook: Economists cautioned that business investment growth, which has been in double digits for three straight quarters, could slow as investors scrutinize AI valuations.
rows.why: GDP가 무엇을 측정하는지, 소비·투자·정부지출이 성장률에 어떻게 기여하는지, 그리고 첫 추정치가 왜 나중에 수정되는지 이해하는 데 도움이 됩니다.
rows.why_en: It shows what GDP measures, how consumption, investment and government spending add up to growth, and why first estimates get revised later.
rows.term_def: A quarter's growth expressed as if it continued at the same pace for a full year, so a roughly 1% rise in one quarter is reported as about 4% annualized; it lets different periods be compared easily.
rows.note: Today's policy item (official BEA data release, GDP second estimate for Q3 2026, Nov 25 ET; not used in the Nov 25 edition). Headline 4.3% (vs 3.4% advance) and Q2 2.2% checked against BEA's GDP release listing dated Nov 25, 2026. Census durable goods for October (+0.2%, released the same day) was also checked but GDP chosen as more significant. Reuters article timestamp 9:28 AM (ET assumed) = Nov 25 KST.

opinion.title: Real GDP Growth Revised Up to 4.3% in the Third Quarter
opinion.author: Mike (Mish) Shedlock
opinion.summary: Shedlock breaks down the BEA's second estimate and argues the 4.3% headline overstates the economy's health. He notes that inventory building (1.64 percentage points) and government spending (0.97 points) together account for about as much as real final sales growth of 2.6%, which he treats as the truer measure. At the same time, he says real final private domestic sales of 5.8% point to an overheating economy, driven by an AI investment boom that is also pulling in imports. He adds that real personal income has barely grown and that tariffs have not shrunk the trade deficit, linking the data to his view that the Fed is behind the curve on rate hikes.
opinion.why: 같은 GDP 숫자라도 재고·정부지출·순수출 같은 구성 요소를 나눠 보면 경제를 다르게 해석할 수 있다는 점을 보여 줍니다.
opinion.why_en: It shows how splitting the same GDP number into parts like inventories, government spending and net exports can lead to a very different reading of the economy.

rows.title: BOK lifts rate to 3.25% as it sharply upgrades growth forecasts through next year
rows.summary: At its last meeting of the year on Nov. 26, the Bank of Korea raised its base rate by 0.25 percentage point to 3.25%. That makes three hikes in 2026, after the ones in July and August, and two of the seven board members voted to hold instead. The bank raised its growth forecast to 3.9% for 2026 (from 3.3%) and to 4.1% for 2027 (from 2.9%), pointing to the strong semiconductor cycle. Inflation is still expected to stay above the 2% target, at 2.7% this year and 2.4% next year. At the same time, the bank cut its 2026 private consumption forecast to 1.8% from 2.1%, so the chip boom is not yet reaching household spending, and Governor Shin Hyun-song said the policymakers' projections for future rates should be taken at face value, leaving room for more hikes.
rows.fact: The BOK raised its key rate 25 basis points to 3.25% in a 5-2 vote, its third hike this year. It lifted its 2027 growth forecast to 4.1%, which would be the fastest growth since 2021, and kept its inflation forecasts above the 2% target. In the board's dot plot of 21 projections, 6 point to 3.25%, 8 to 3.5% and 7 to 3.75%.
rows.outlook: Morgan Stanley's Kathleen Oh now expects a higher peak rate than before, with hikes to 3.5% in February 2027 and 3.75% in the third quarter of 2027.
rows.why: 경제가 빠르게 성장하고 물가가 목표치를 웃돌 때 중앙은행이 왜 금리를 올리는지, 그리고 반도체 호황과 위축된 가계 소비가 어떻게 함께 나타날 수 있는지 이해하는 데 도움이 됩니다.
rows.why_en: It shows why a central bank raises rates when growth is strong and inflation stays above target, and how a chip export boom can coexist with weak household spending.
rows.term_def: A chart showing where each member of the central bank's policy board expects the interest rate to be in the future. It gives the public a hint about the likely path of rates.
rows.note: Today's policy item (Bank of Korea Monetary Policy Board decision, Nov 26 KST). The rate, the 5-2 vote, the July/August hikes and the growth and inflation forecasts were cross-checked against the Korea Herald (Choi Yeon-jae, Nov 26), AP (via WSLS) and Investing.com reporting on the same day, and they match. The official BOK English homepage still showed 3.00% and the Oct 22 decision when fetched, probably because it had not been updated yet, so the numbers rest on agreement among those outlets. Not a repeat: the items covered earlier this week were sentiment surveys, exports, stocks and producer prices, not this rate decision.

opinion.title: BOK sees economy running hot, households remain cold
opinion.author: Kim Yeon-jae
opinion.summary: This analysis sets the BOK's rosy forecasts, driven by about 700 trillion won in expected operating profits at Samsung Electronics and SK hynix, against data showing households under strain. Real household income fell 2.1% from a year earlier in the third quarter, the first drop in 10 quarters. Self-employed business income shrank, overdue loans by individual business owners jumped 21.5%, and the average rate on new household loans topped 5% in October. Governor Shin argued that chip profits will reach ordinary households through taxes, bonuses and dividends over time, while a Meritz Securities analyst said markets still need to see that growth actually happen and that the two dissenting votes reflect worries about growth concentrated in chips.
opinion.why: GDP 성장률이 높아도 그 혜택이 특정 산업에 집중되면 가계 소득과 소비는 오히려 줄어들 수 있으며, 금리 인상이 빚을 진 가계와 자영업자에게 어떤 부담을 주는지 생각해 볼 수 있습니다.
opinion.why_en: It shows that high GDP growth concentrated in one industry can leave household income and spending falling, and makes you weigh what a rate hike costs indebted families and small business owners.

rows.title: ECB already had large support for rate hike in Oct, accounts show
rows.summary: The European Central Bank on Thursday published the accounts (minutes) of its October 28-29 meeting, showing that policymakers in Frankfurt were already leaning toward raising interest rates but chose to wait for more evidence on inflation risks. Many members said data since September confirmed the case for further tightening and that they could have backed a hike in October, while the bank warned inflation could run higher than previously expected. Oil and gas prices are well above the ECB's baseline scenario and low gas storage means a cold winter could lift utility bills, so policymakers want to prevent 'second-round effects', where energy costs spread into wages and other prices. Most officials who have spoken since have signalled a 25-basis-point hike on December 17, which Reuters calls almost a done deal, but the path after that is unclear because union wage talks are unfinished, the labour market is softer than in 2022 and energy prices have recently eased. The debate will soon pass to new leadership, as President Christine Lagarde and board member Isabel Schnabel leave in the coming months.
rows.fact: Accounts of the ECB's Oct 28-29 meeting, released Nov 26, show a large number of policymakers could have supported a rate hike in October, describing such a move as merely bringing forward tightening that is needed anyway. The ECB held its deposit rate at 2.50% in October, and most officials have since signalled a quarter-point hike on December 17.
rows.outlook: Reuters reports a December hike is nearly certain, but further hikes are less urgent because second-round effects have not appeared, the labour market is softer than in 2022 and energy prices have fallen back from near-'severe' scenario levels.
rows.why: 중앙은행이 에너지 가격 상승이 임금과 다른 물가로 번지는 '2차 효과'를 막기 위해 왜 미리 금리를 올리려 하는지, 그리고 회의록이 앞으로의 금리 결정을 어떻게 예고하는지 이해하는 데 도움이 됩니다.
rows.why_en: It shows why a central bank may raise rates pre-emptively to stop an energy price shock from spreading into wages and other prices, and how meeting minutes signal future rate decisions.
rows.term_def: When an initial price shock (like higher oil and gas prices) causes workers to demand higher wages and firms to raise other prices, turning a one-time jump into lasting, broader inflation.
rows.note: Today's policy item (ECB publication of the October 28-29 monetary policy meeting accounts, Nov 26 CET; Reuters story by Balazs Koranyi, Frankfurt dateline). Article body read in full on Investing.com and a second Reuters republication (Global Banking & Finance Review). Rate levels cross-checked against the ECB's Oct 29, 2026 press release (deposit facility 2.50%, MRO 2.65%, marginal lending 2.90%, all unchanged). The ECB's own accounts page could not be located, so details of the accounts rely on Reuters. Not a repeat: the 7-day list covers eurozone Oct inflation and the ECB Financial Stability Review was not used.

opinion.title: European Central Bank: December hike seen as almost certain
opinion.author: Anders Svendsen, Nordea (via FXStreet Insights Team)
opinion.summary: Nordea analyst Anders Svendsen argues that a December ECB rate hike is almost a given, as markets have it nearly fully priced and Governing Council members' recent comments point the same way. He notes markets price close to 60 basis points of further hikes on top of the 50 basis points delivered in June and September, and reads Lagarde's October hint partly as a response to widening French bond spreads tightening financial conditions. Nordea still expects four hikes in total in this cycle, with the remaining two now pencilled in for December and March. He adds that once the inflation peak comes into view in 2027, markets could start shifting from pricing hikes toward pricing rate cuts.
opinion.why: 금융시장이 앞으로의 금리 인상을 미리 가격에 반영하는 방식과, 물가 정점이 보이면 금리 전망이 인상에서 인하로 바뀔 수 있다는 점을 배울 수 있습니다.
opinion.why_en: It shows how markets 'price in' expected rate hikes in advance and why expectations can flip from hikes to cuts once inflation is seen peaking.

rows.title: BOJ policymaker signals chance of faster-pace interest rate hikes
rows.summary: Naoki Tamura, one of the most hawkish members of the Bank of Japan's nine-member policy board, said on Thursday that the central bank must react quickly to signs that inflation is overshooting, including by speeding up its interest rate hikes. He pointed to higher raw material and crude oil costs linked to the Middle East conflict, a weak yen that makes imports more expensive, and strong demand for AI-related goods as sources of upside price risk. Because financial conditions in Japan are still loose, he argued the BOJ needs to bring its 1.25% policy rate up to a 'neutral' level soon, and said Japan's less firmly anchored inflation expectations mean the bank must respond to shocks more swiftly and strongly than other central banks. The BOJ has already raised rates in June and September, a faster pace than the roughly twice-a-year hikes of 2024 and 2025, and markets widely expect another move to 1.5% at its December 17-18 meeting. Faster hikes would mean higher borrowing costs in Japan, with effects on the yen, government bond yields and a fragile economy where consumption has been soft.
rows.fact: BOJ board member Naoki Tamura said in a speech on Nov 26 that the bank should respond swiftly to an inflation overshoot, possibly by accelerating rate hikes, and bring its policy rate to neutral soon. He said the current 1.25% rate is still some way from neutral given accommodative financial conditions, and that the BOJ can judge the effects of each hike within a few months.
rows.outlook: Markets widely expect the BOJ to raise its policy rate from 1.25% to 1.5% when its two-day meeting ends on December 18.
rows.why: 물가가 목표치를 넘어설 위험이 있을 때 중앙은행이 왜 금리 인상 속도를 높이려 하는지, 그리고 '중립금리'와 엔화 약세가 일본 통화정책에 어떤 영향을 주는지 이해하는 데 도움이 됩니다.
rows.why_en: It shows why a central bank may speed up rate hikes when inflation risks rise, and how the idea of a 'neutral' rate and a weak yen shape Japan's monetary policy.
rows.term_def: The interest rate level that neither speeds up nor slows down the economy; if the policy rate is below it, monetary policy is still stimulating spending and borrowing.
rows.note: Today's policy item (BOJ board member Naoki Tamura's speech to local leaders in Yamanashi, Nov 26 JST, reported by Reuters). The 1.25% policy rate, the June and September hikes and the Dec 17-18 meeting were confirmed across the Reuters article, the investingLive Asia calendar for Nov 26 (which listed Tamura's 10:00 JST Yamanashi speech) and a second Reuters piece. The Standard's page shows a relative time ('22 mins ago') with no explicit date; the Nov 26 date comes from the 'on Thursday' wording and the calendar. The speech was not yet on the BOJ's English speeches page when checked (latest listed was Takata, Nov 16), and fetching the BOJ Japanese speech page timed out, so the speech text itself was not cross-checked against the official source. Bloomberg's version (paywalled) was not used.

opinion.title: Analysis-BOJ's ambiguity on rate hike path could tempt yen bears
opinion.author: Leika Kihara
opinion.summary: This Reuters analysis argues that BOJ policymakers broadly agree on hiking in December but disagree on how high rates should ultimately go, and that this missing endpoint could keep the yen weak even as the bank tightens. BOJ staff estimate the neutral rate somewhere between 1.1% and 2.5%, with hawks such as Tamura (around 2%) and Takata at the higher end, while markets see tightening ending near 1.75%-2%. Analysts quoted say the yen's direction will largely decide how far the BOJ goes, and that US rate hikes keep pressure on Japan to raise rates too. The piece also notes that Tamura's and Takata's terms end in July, giving Prime Minister Takaichi a chance to reshape the board.
opinion.why: 중앙은행이 금리의 '최종 도착점'을 분명히 밝히지 않으면 환율과 시장 기대가 어떻게 흔들리는지 보여 주어, 소통(포워드 가이던스)이 통화정책에서 왜 중요한지 배울 수 있습니다.
opinion.why_en: It shows how unclear signals about where rates will end up can move the currency and market expectations, teaching why central bank communication matters.
